I'm sure you have all heard of ChatGPT by now. It has become a buzzword within days of its release and professionals in all fields, especially in high skilled areas like lawyers, doctors, engineers are questioning whether such AI can actually replace them and work.

So in this video I want to talk about what ChatGPT is and how it even popped up, talk a bit about the organization behind GPT called "OpenAI", which has already created many other machine learning models besides Chat GPT and also explain technically about all that.
And then we'll dive in and actually put ChatGPT to use for some DevOps related tasks.
I really want to see how it can help in generating configuration code for building DevOps processes or different parts of those processes and how well it knows different DevOps technologies, but not just some shallow examples or boilerplate code that I can get from official documentation, but instead also try more fine-tuning and small optimizations in that configuration code.

We're also going to check out an open source command line tool that is built on top of ChatGPT and was specifically created for engineers to generate infrastructure as code templates and more and finally we'll talk about the impact of ChatGPT, the quality and usefulness of such a tool for engineers and whether it will really replace the engineers and to what extent you should be concerned.

Edureka’s DevOps online training is designed to help you master key tools of Devops lifecycle like Docker, Puppet, Jenkins, Nagios, GIT, Ansible, SaltStack and Chef used by a DevOps Engineer for automating multiple steps in SDLC. During this course, our expert DevOps instructors will help you:

videoTitle: The ONLY Roadmap to Get a DevOps Job in 2026 | Zero to Hero Guidance | Senior DevOps Engineer | USA
videoDescription:
This is the exact roadmap that will get you hired in 2026. 🚀

Stop following random roadmaps that leave you more confused than when you started. The DevOps landscape is shifting, and simply knowing a few tools isn't enough anymore. To land a high-paying role today, you need to understand the logic, the architecture, and the "why" behind every deployment.

videoTitle: What is Platform Engineering and how it fits into DevOps and Cloud world
videoDescription:
Platform Engineering - What it is, how it works and how it fits into DevOps and Cloud world
Also how to approach implementing an IDP - internal developer platform.

🔗💚   Become a DevOps Engineer in 6 months       ►   https://bit.ly/3WKUPGf
🔗💙   Become a Kubernetes Administrator              ►   https://bit.ly/3IMJUWI
🔗🧡   Complete GitLab CI/CD course                        ►   https://bit.ly/42itb4B
🔗 💜  DevSecOps Bootcamp                                       ►   https://bit.ly/3OI6y66

▬▬▬▬▬▬ Thank you Pulumi for sponsoring this video 👏  ▬▬▬▬▬▬
►   Learn more about Pulumi's Internal developer platform-in-a-box: https://pulumip.us/IDP-Platform-Engineering
►   Join PulumiUp - a global Infrastructure as Code conference: https://www.pulumi.com/pulumi-up/

In this video we're going to talk about a relatively new hot topic in DevOps and Cloud space, which is “platform engineering”. There is a lot of discussion going on, where some people are asking whether platform engineering replaces DevOps. Many people say it goes hand in hand and is rather an addition to DevOps, but in reality it's a bit more complicated than that. Platform engineering actually changes a lot of established rules we knew about DevOps, SRE and Cloud engineering, it changes the game and introduces some new rules.

So let's clearly define, what platform engineering exactly is, more interestingly, why was there even a need for this new role and how it evolved and of course how it compares to DevOps and Cloud engineering and does it really replace any of these roles?

videoTitle: 보이지 않는 다리, DevOps: 개발과 운영을 잇는 IT 세상의 숨고르기
videoDescription:
여러분은 하루 중 언제 쉬시나요?
저는 퇴근길 지하철에서 다리를 건너며 노을을 바라볼 때, 잠시 숨을 고릅니다.
IT 세계에도 이런 보이지 않는 다리가 있습니다. 바로 DevOps입니다.

DevOps는 Development(개발)과 Operations(운영)을 하나로 잇는 문화와 방법론입니다.
개발자가 새로운 기능을 만들고, 운영팀이 서버를 관리하던 과거에는 늘 벽이 있었습니다.
하지만 DevOps는 이 벽을 허물어, 서비스가 더 빠르고 안정적으로 배포되도록 합니다.

✨ DevOps 핵심 개념

자동화: 코드 작성 → 빌드 → 테스트 → 배포까지 자동 처리

CI/CD: 작은 기능도 자주, 안정적으로 배포

모니터링과 피드백: 실시간으로 문제 감지 & 개선

도구 활용: Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes, Prometheus, Grafana

이제 DevOps는 클라우드와 만나 더 강력해졌습니다.
코드 한 줄 수정이 전 세계에 즉시 반영되는 CI/CD 파이프라인.
서버리스, API 게이트웨이, 컨테이너를 통한 마이크로서비스 아키텍처.
그리고 AI와 결합해 데이터 처리, 보안, 모델 최적화까지 개발자가 직접 다루는 시대가 되었습니다.

카카오톡이 멈추지 않고, 넷플릭스가 전 세계 수억 명에게 끊김 없이 영상을 제공할 수 있는 이유.
그 중심에는 항상 DevOps와 클라우드가 있습니다.

눈에 잘 띄지 않지만, 없으면 모든 게 멈추는 다리.
그게 바로 DevOps입니다.

오늘 영상이 도움이 되셨다면,
구독과 좋아요, 알림 설정으로 함께해주세요 🙌

Complete CI/CD with Terraform
Integrate the provisioning stage into the complete CI/CD Pipeline to automate the provisioning server instead of deploying it to an existing server

- Create SSH Key Pair
- Install Terraform inside Github Actions runner
- Add Terraform configuration to the application’s git repository
- Adjust GH actions workflow to add a “provision” step to the CI/CD pipeline that provisions EC2
instance
- So the complete CI/CD project we build has the following configuration:
CI step: Build and push Docker image to AWS ECR
CD step: Automatically provision EC2 instance using TF
CD step: Deploy the new application version on the provisioned EC2 instance with the docker

videoTitle: DevOps Meetup Zurich 2024: Platform Engineering
videoDescription:
This video captures my presentation delivered at the DevOps Meetup in Zürich on January 25, 2024, where I delve into the prevalent challenges faced by traditional DevOps methodologies, characterized by isolated teams and fragmented value streams that impede efficiency. It explores DevOps as a holistic culture, mindset, and suite of technical practices designed to foster continuous value delivery, prioritize products over projects, and focus on customer-centric development. Additionally, I introduce Platform Engineering as a strategic evolution of DevOps aimed at mitigating the technical and operational complexities encountered when scaling DevOps in larger enterprises. Highlighting a collaborative project with LGT and Zühlke, I present the Platform Plane case study, demonstrating how an internal developer platform can streamline and standardize DevOps processes across various teams, thereby reducing cognitive load and enhancing productivity. This presentation goes beyond theoretical discussion, offering a hands-on demonstration of the Platform Plane and its functionalities, including Kubernetes as a service, API gateway, and Service Mesh, among others. It illustrates the vital role of Platform Engineering in enabling product teams to adopt DevOps more efficiently and effectively, leading to an optimized development lifecycle.

Unito supports essential fields in Azure DevOps and Jira, including:

📝 Description: The detailed description of the issue or work item, including any additional information or context needed for team members to understand the task.

👤 Assignee: The person responsible for completing the task or addressing the issue. Keeping the assignee field in sync ensures that the correct team member is aware of their responsibilities.

🔢 Status: The current status of the issue or work item, such as "To Do," "In Progress," or "Done." Syncing the status field helps everyone stay updated on the progress of tasks.

🔝 Priority: The priority level of the issue or work item, which helps determine its importance and urgency. Syncing the priority field ensures that team members are aligned on task prioritization.

🏷️ Labels/Tags: Categorizing issues or work items with labels or tags helps with organization and filtering. Keeping these fields in sync ensures consistent labeling across both platforms.

💬 Comments/Updates: Any comments or updates made on an issue or work item should be synced to provide real-time collaboration and visibility for everyone involved.

⏰ Due Date: If there is a specific deadline or due date associated with the task or issue, syncing this field helps the team stay on track and meet deadlines.

📎 Attachments: Any files or attachments related to the issue or work item should be synced to ensure easy access and collaboration.

📌 Work Item Type/Issue Type: The type of work item or issue, such as bug, feature, or task. Syncing this field provides clarity and consistency in categorizing different types of work.

videoTitle: ♾️🛠️CI/CD Pipeline Explained in Tamil🔁 | #thillaithetechie
videoDescription:
✅ Continuous Integration (CI):
✅ CI is a development practice where code changes are automatically built, tested, and integrated into a shared repository multiple times a day.
✅ It ensures early detection of integration errors and promotes collaboration among developers by providing rapid feedback on code changes.

✅ Continuous Delivery (CD):
✅ CD extends CI by automating the deployment process, enabling teams to release software changes to production or staging environments quickly and reliably.
✅ It streamlines the deployment pipeline, reduces manual intervention, and enhances the consistency and repeatability of software releases.

✅ Pipeline Automation:
✅ CI/CD pipelines automate various stages of the software delivery process, including code compilation, testing, artifact creation, and deployment.
✅ Automated pipelines ensure consistency, efficiency, and reliability, allowing teams to focus on delivering value-added features and improvements.

✅ Feedback Loop:
✅ CI/CD pipelines incorporate feedback loops at each stage, enabling teams to identify and address issues promptly, iterate on solutions, and continuously improve software quality and performance.

✅ DevOps Culture:
✅ CI/CD practices are integral to the DevOps culture, fostering collaboration between development and operations teams, breaking down silos, and promoting a culture of continuous improvement and innovation.

videoTitle: Steps to Enable Parallel Jobs In Azure DevOps (AZ-400)
videoDescription:
All you will get information in this Video: https://youtu.be/DBQLl360Mz0

Purpose of Parallel Jobs: The video explains how to enable parallel jobs in Azure DevOps, which is necessary for running CI/CD pipelines.

Creating a Project: Start by creating a project within your Azure DevOps organization, noting your organization URL.

Access Billing Settings: Navigate to the organization settings, select "Billing," and locate the option for parallel jobs.

Parallel Jobs Availability: Initially, new organizations have zero parallel jobs available, preventing pipeline execution until jobs are enabled.

Requesting Parallel Jobs: Users must request parallel jobs through a specific URL provided by Microsoft, as they no longer provide them by default due to past misuse.

Misuse Prevention: Microsoft stopped offering free parallel jobs by default because users exploited them for unauthorized activities like Bitcoin mining.

Request Process: Fill out the form with your name, the same email ID used for Azure DevOps, and your organization URL. Request only private parallel jobs unless you have a valid reason for public jobs.

Approval Timeframe: It typically takes 24 to 48 hours for Microsoft to approve parallel job requests.

Verification: After approval, you can verify the availability of parallel jobs in the Azure DevOps portal under the "Parallel Jobs" section in the billing settings.

Billing Setup for Additional Jobs: For additional parallel jobs, users need an active Azure subscription (e.g., Pay-As-You-Go), and setup billing, linking it to the Azure subscription. This will allow for purchasing more parallel jobs if needed.

videoTitle: BTAIH E03 · Mohamed Daoudi, DevOps Engineer · Can AI Replace DevOps Engineers?
videoDescription:
My third guest on BTAIH is Mohamed Daoudi, a DevOps engineer whose path took him from ENSA and self-taught Linux and Docker to early-stage companies, large-scale cloud systems at Oracle, and independent consulting.

We get into what happens when AI stops being a chatbot and starts touching real infrastructure: writing scripts, handling repetitive migrations, executing commands, configuring CI/CD, connecting hosting and domains, and helping ship a working website in less than 24 hours.

It is a practical conversation, not a hype one. Where AI genuinely makes a DevOps engineer faster, where it turns 100 lines into 10,000, and why giving an agent access to your systems is only useful when you still understand the infrastructure underneath it.

About Mohamed

Mohamed Daoudi is a DevOps engineer with experience across startups, service companies, Oracle Cloud and independent consulting. His work has included CI/CD, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, incident management and keeping production systems stable at scale.

✓ How to deploy and access a local development VHD using Hyper-V.
✓ Authenticate the local VM using Azure App Registration.

──────────────────────────
🚀 About This D365 Development Series
──────────────────────────

This series goes beyond basic tutorials to show you how real-world Dynamics 365 (D365FO) projects are built from start to finish. We'll build a complete, end-to-end "Automated Customer Tiering System" for a fictional client, Bluestone Industrial Components (BIC).

You'll see every step of a production-ready solution, from setup to deployment, covering:
➤ Core X++ Development: Extending tables and forms (CustTable), creating Enums, and implementing custom business logic using Chain of Command (CoC).
➤ Automation: Building robust, automated batch jobs with the SysOperation Framework.
➤ APIs & Integration: Creating Data Entities to build secure OData REST APIs and for Data Management Framework (DMF) exports.
➤ Event-Driven Architecture: Firing real-time alerts from D365 to Azure Logic Apps using Business Events.
➤ Business Intelligence: Connecting D365 to Power BI to build an interactive sales dashboard.
➤ DevOps & ALM: Setting up a complete CI/CD pipeline in Azure DevOps, managing source control (TFVC), and automating builds.

🔹Visual Studio 2019
🔹Lifecycle Services (LCS)
🔹Azure DevOps (ADO)
🔹SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)

───────────────────

videoTitle: InFocus - Honeycomb: Accept Code is Never Going to Be Perfect #LaunchDarkly #DevOps #FeatureFlags
videoDescription:
I used to be on call 24/7 as a team lead, no vacations, no unplugging. All because of one big lie: that software could be perfect before it hits production.

Reality? It never is.

What actually matters isn’t perfect code. It’s having control. The ability to roll back instantly, fix fast, and adapt when things go wrong.

That’s the shift: from chasing perfection to building confidence in change.
channelDescription:
LaunchDarkly is the runtime control layer for the AI era. For over a decade we have helped engineering teams control what ships in production, from feature flags to full release governance. Today that mission extends to the AI agents and code that are increasingly building, modifying, and operating software on behalf of engineering teams.

With CodeControl and AgentControl, teams can ship faster, govern what runs in production, and automatically respond when something needs to change, without waiting on a redeploy. Why DevOps is not dying, but evolving into specialized domains

The real difference between DevOps, MLOps, AIOps, and DataOps

──────────────────────────
🚀 About This D365 Development Series
──────────────────────────

This series goes beyond basic tutorials to show you how real-world Dynamics 365 (D365FO) projects are built from start to finish. We'll build a complete, end-to-end "Automated Customer Tiering System" for a fictional client, Bluestone Industrial Components (BIC).

You'll see every step of a production-ready solution, from setup to deployment, covering:
➤ Core X++ Development: Extending tables and forms (CustTable), creating Enums, and implementing custom business logic using Chain of Command (CoC).
➤ Automation: Building robust, automated batch jobs with the SysOperation Framework.
➤ APIs & Integration: Creating Data Entities to build secure OData REST APIs and for Data Management Framework (DMF) exports.
➤ Event-Driven Architecture: Firing real-time alerts from D365 to Azure Logic Apps using Business Events.
➤ Business Intelligence: Connecting D365 to Power BI to build an interactive sales dashboard.
➤ DevOps & ALM: Setting up a complete CI/CD pipeline in Azure DevOps, managing source control (TFVC), and automating builds.

🔹X++
🔹Visual Studio 2019
🔹Lifecycle Services (LCS)
🔹Azure DevOps (ADO)
🔹SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS)
🔹Power BI Desktop

───────────────────
💬 Feedback & Future Topics

videoTitle: The DevOps Godfather on AI's "Dark Factory" Problem
videoDescription:
Organizations are resisting the 'dark factory' model, not because of a lack of technological capability, but due to unprepared structures and mindsets. Coding agents are ready, but companies aren't set up for their seamless integration. Just like continuous delivery faced skepticism in 2009, autonomous coding agents now challenge existing frameworks and require a paradigm shift from developers as coders to orchestrators of systems. The shift isn't about better technology; it's about rethinking the roles and processes within an organization. Developers must evolve from technical craftsmanship to a conductor role in a system-driven environment, changing how teams and platforms function.

Patrick Debois, known widely as the 'godfather of DevOps', brings unique insights to this discussion. Having witnessed similar skepticism with the continuous delivery movement, Debois now observes the parallels between the challenges faced then and the resistance faced by the 'dark factory' approach today. At Tessl, where he observes first-hand the dynamics of adopting autonomous code agents, he highlights how this shift influences collaboration, team dynamics, and the role of platform teams.

videoTitle: How We Fixed a 502 Bad Gateway in Production | Real DevOps Incident (Day 7)
videoDescription:

Scenario:
Production just went down with a 502 Bad Gateway after a critical deployment. Jenkins pipeline triggered it, the deployment failed — and users were impacted.

🎯 Here’s how we handled it in real time:

Checked logs — the app was failing health checks

Root cause: a missing production environment variable

Rolled back the deployment safely using Helm

Fixed the configuration and stopped further rollouts

Patched the CI/CD pipeline to catch such issues early

🎥 Watch this short video to learn how real DevOps teams fix issues fast under pressure — and how you can too.

Handling incidents is not just about tools — it’s about staying calm, investigating smartly, and improving your pipeline for the future.

videoTitle: Kubernetes at Mercedes-Benz | Philipp Bormann & Jens Erat | The DEVOPS Conference - Copenhagen, 2022
videoDescription:
How did Kubernetes change the game for software engineers at Mercedes-Benz?

Years ago, software engineers faced hard times at Mercedes-Benz: spreadsheet operations, manual processes, grown infrastructure, and strict governance. A grassroots initiative of engineers accepted the challenge to change the game – and their silver bullet was Kubernetes.

Join us on our journey from introducing Kubernetes 0.9 on managed servers to an on-premises self-service cloud platform with close to 1000 clusters on Cluster API. You will learn about our stake in transforming a data center with a young team that mostly did not know enterprise processes before.

We will take you back on our journey, including some technical details about the challenges we faced, our solutions to those, and lessons learned on the way.
---

Philipp Bormann, Platform Architect at Mercedes-Benz Group AG

videoTitle: Manage & Secure Kubernetes Cluster Policies via OPA Gatekeeper. #opa #devops #gatekeeper
videoDescription:
Manage & Secure Kubernetes Cluster Policies via OPA Gatekeeper. #opa #devops #gatekeepers 

Timestamps:

Theory/Concepts : 00:00
Hands on/Practical : 09:00

github repo : https://github.com/RohanRusta21/opa-gatekeeper.git

Concepts :

OPA Gatekeeper: Policy and Governance for Kubernetes

What is OPA:

The Open Policy Agent (OPA) is an open-source, general-purpose policy engine that unifies policy enforcement across the stack. OPA provides a high-level declarative language that lets us specify policies as code and simple APIs to offload policy decision-making from our software. We can use OPA to enforce policies in microservices, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, API gateways, and more. 
In kubernetes, OPA uses admission controllers.

What is OPA Gatekeeper?

OPA Gatekeeper is a specialized project providing first-class integration between OPA and Kubernetes.
OPA Gatekeeper adds the following on top of plain OPA:
● An extensible, parameterized policy library.
● Native Kubernetes CRDs for instantiating the policy library (aka “constraints”).
● Native Kubernetes CRDs for extending the policy library (aka “constraint templates”).
● Audit functionality.

Why you need Gatekeeper?

As a Platform DevOps engineer managing multiple Kubernetes clusters for various projects, you face challenges when users deploy applications without adhering to best practices. Key issues include:
  1.     Lack of ownership unless users apply labels themselves.
  2.     No resource limits, leading to high costs.
  3.     Untrusted images impacting other applications.
  4.     Security and best practice violations across clusters.

To address these, we need governance to enforce limits and rules via policies. OPA Gatekeeper can be configured to implement these policies, ensuring best practices are followed.

videoTitle: Is your multicloud pipeline compliant? DevOps vs GitOps
videoDescription:
DevOps Isn't Enough: GitOps Strategies for Regulated Multicloud Deployments

Sujeily Fonseca-Gonzalez walks through how GitOps practices and Argo CD make multicloud compliance manageable for regulated environments like FedRAMP, HIPAA, and Protected B. Learn how git becomes your audit trail, how evidence lockers automate proof of compliance, and how Argo CD's built-in RBAC, sync policies, and audit logging map to regulated deployment requirements across AWS, IBM, and Google Cloud.

Summary: 
Your project's direct dependencies are the easy part. Viral Chhasatia walks through dependency auditing across Python, npm, Maven, Go, Rust, and Docker using tools like pip licenses, CycloneDX, npm license checker, go licenses, cargo about, and Sift. Learn why transitive dependencies carry hidden license risks, why your SBOM is already outdated, and why no single tool gives you the complete picture.

Session: Bridging DevOps And GitOps: MultiCloud Strategies For HyperScalers

GitOps has transformed the way organizations manage cloud-native applications, but scaling it across federal and commercial hyperscalers presents unique challenges. In this session, Sujeily Fonseca-Gonzalez will share lessons learned from leading GitOps implementations in highly regulated environments, covering best practices for security, compliance, automation, and scalability. Attendees will gain insights into key differences between federal and commercial cloud GitOps workflows, overcoming security and compliance hurdles in highly regulated environments, enhancing CI/CD pipelines for resilience, observability, and automation, and lessons from real-world implementations, including multi-cloud strategies and open source technologies.



Learn more about GitOps strategies for complex multi-cloud deployment environments. Sujeily Fonseca-Gonzalez explains how to manage infrastructure consistency across hyperscalers.

This session breaks down the technical transition from DevOps to GitOps, specifically addressing the challenges of tool fragmentation and security in distributed systems. If you are an engineer or architect managing infrastructure, this overview provides clarity on maintaining compliance while scaling operations across different platforms.

Learn to overcome common hurdles when implementing GitOps strategies at scale. The discussion covers practical lessons from real-world multi-cloud deployment scenarios, focusing on how to maintain security standards and operational consistency. By the end, you will understand the necessary architectural shifts required for successful cloud infrastructure management.

videoTitle: Why DevOps transformations fail in regulated industries, with Merge Ready's Matt Bailey
videoDescription:
https://cortex.io/

00:00 Why DevOps is an outcome, not a toolchain.
02:47 How compliance can be automated instead of blocking delivery.
14:25 Automating GitLab CI/CD approvals through ServiceNow workflows.
22:08 Starting DevOps transformations with pilot teams and controls as code.
27:07 Why stakeholder management is a core DevOps skill.
32:43 How AI changes DevOps and the case for ClickOps.

Cortex co-founder and CTO Ganesh Datta sits down with Matt Bailey, DevOps consultant and founder of Merge Ready. Matt shares lessons from helping large regulated organizations in finance, healthcare, and government transform their DevOps practices, and explains why DevOps is an outcome rather than a toolchain.

Matt and Ganesh discuss why compliance can be mostly automated rather than a mandatory bottleneck, how to turn 30-day approval processes into continuous audit readiness through controls as code, and why treating platform teams as product teams drives natural adoption. They also explore decision latency as a core organizational problem, the importance of stakeholder management as a DevOps skill, and how AI agents may shift infrastructure drift management from prevention to embrace.

videoTitle: DevOps Hands-On | Ansible – Day 4  ( DevOpsFarm Day 46 )
videoDescription:
In this in-depth session, we dive into the critical world of DevOps monitoring and master the industry-leading open-source tools: Grafana, Prometheus, and Loki.

Learn why monitoring is essential for getting system feedback, taking proactive action, and preventing system failure due to issues like high CPU usage, low RAM, or disk space depletion. We cover the key aspects you must monitor, including system resources, logs, and traces.




What you will learn in this session:


The Importance of Monitoring: Understand the benefits, including anomaly detection, generating alerts, and creating useful dashboards for historical data analysis.



Core Monitoring Tools: An overview of popular tools like Grafana, New Relic, Datadog, and Dynatrace.



Prometheus Explained: A deep dive into Prometheus, the time-series database used for collecting and tracking metrics (like CPU usage over time).



Loki for Logging: Learn how Loki is used for log collection and parsing, making logs consumable by Grafana.



The Grafana Stack in Action: See how Grafana serves as the visualization layer, consuming data from Prometheus and Loki to create powerful dashboards and configure alerts.



Practical Demo: We demonstrate connecting data sources, exploring metrics using PromQL, and setting up label-based notification policies to ensure the right teams are alerted instantly.


Whether you are a beginner or a seasoned DevOps professional, this guide provides the knowledge and practical steps needed to implement robust monitoring for any application or microservice environment.

videoTitle: 20260325 Building a DevOps Pipeline with Cloud Build Trigger on Google Cloud Platform
videoDescription:
👉 This demo walks through how to build a DevOps pipeline on Google Cloud Platform using a Cloud Build trigger that automatically runs whenever code is pushed to a GitHub repository. When triggered, it deploys a simple Flask application to a VM instance, where users can access a “Hello Build Trigger” webpage over HTTP or HTTPS. The entire workflow is defined in the cloudbuild.yaml file.

Step 1. The pipeline begins by detecting the active project and determining the allowed region and zones, ensuring that all resources are created in the correct and permitted environment.

Step 2. It then builds a Docker image for the Flask application using the source code from the repository, preparing it for deployment.

Step 3. Next, the pipeline either creates a new VM instance or updates an existing one. It installs Docker, Nginx, and OpenSSL, runs the Docker container for the Flask app, generates a self-signed SSL certificate, and configures Nginx as a reverse proxy to handle HTTPS traffic. If the VM already exists, it skips the setup and simply redeploys the updated image.

Step 4. Finally, it sets up firewall rules to allow incoming HTTP and HTTPS traffic, making the application accessible from the internet.

videoTitle: Heather Thacker - DevOps and Baking
videoDescription:
Baking from a box mix requires little thought and usually yields good results, while assembling a cake from scratch can fall flat from inaccurate measurements or miscalculated techniques. Let’s explore the limitations of DevOps solutions that are offered out of the box versus built from scratch.

This talk is a comparison of my past profession with my current one. Looking at stages of baking in preparing, mixing, baking, and selling while comparing to DevOps stages of planning, building, deploying, and feedback. And disaster recovery! A look into what is needed when bread is burnt, a retroactive consideration of steps necessary to address disasters and how to recover.

We will go over recipes for success and how to be creative with customizing recipes and methodologies. Efficiency of processes will be considered and how to maintain this while adapting to changes and unexpected variables. The audience will gain freshly baked insights into managing DevOps infrastructures through a sweet theme.

videoTitle: The Difference Between DevOps Engineers, System Administrators, and IT Technicians (Desktop Support)
videoDescription:
After watching this video, you will find out who IT technicians, sysadmins, and system engineers are. Why is there so much hype around DevOps right now? How do engineers differ from administrators? And what highly specialized professions are system administrators divided into?

Timestamps:
0:00 Intro
1:07 IT technicians a.k.a. Desktop Support Engineers & Administrators
2:49 System Engineers & Administrators
4:38 Network Engineers & Administrators
6:07 Information Security Specialists a.k.a. Cyber Security Engineers
7:13 DevOps Engineers
9:27 Things To Remember

IT technicians (also known as Desktop Support Engineers) in most organizations are responsible for laptops, PBXs, printers, scanners, etc.

System engineers are responsible for complex IT systems design, and administrators work with the existing systems. Both are more about networks, servers, and other complex hardware.

In large organizations, the aspects of system administration are often divided into narrow specializations: networks, web administration, information security.

DevOps engineers are indispensable persons in companies with development teams and continuous integration (online games, streaming platforms, large retailers, and other services with an audience of thousands). They are responsible for smooth development, testing, and deployment.

videoTitle: Git Plumbing vs Porcelain #Git #GitHub #GitLab #BitBucket #DevOps #GitOps #Python #Java #JavaScript
videoDescription:
Have you heart the terms Git plumbing and Git Porcelain?

Ever wondered what the different between Git porcelain vs plumbing was?

For the most part, the porcelain is the most commonly used Git files such as:

- git init
- git add
- git commit
- git revert
- git merge
- git rebase
- git reset

That's the Git porcelain, and you won't get your hands too dirty when you touch it.

The Git plumbing? That's typically the config stuff in the hidden .git folder, including things like:

- Refspec
-Packfiles
- The HEAD Pointer
- Git References
- Remote References
- Transfer Protocols
- Garbage Collector
- Recovery files
- Tree Objects
- Environment variables

Hopefully you don't have to get your hands dirty with the Git plumbing too often. It's nice to stick with the Git porcelain.

But at the same time, plumbers do make a lot of money!

videoTitle: Deleting the .env doesn't delete the key #git
videoDescription:
You committed a .env, noticed, ran git rm, added it to .gitignore and committed the fix. Working tree clean. The key is still in the repo.

  git log -p --all -- .env | grep API_KEY
  -API_KEY=sk-live-9f3a2b
  +API_KEY=sk-live-9f3a2b

Deleting a file ADDS a commit. It does not edit the old one. Git keeps every commit, and the blob stays an object in the repo:

  git rev-list --objects --all | grep .env
  64bfdcb .env

So anyone who has cloned, forked, or pulled already has it. So does every CI cache and every GitHub fork.

The fix, in this order:
1. Rotate the key. Assume it is already public.
2. Then rewrite history (git filter-repo, or BFG) and force-push.

Step 2 without step 1 is theatre.

Check your own repo in ten seconds:
  git log --all --oneline -- .env

Tested on git 2.46.2, August 2026. Every line of output here is real. Narration is AI-generated.

videoTitle: Why your Claude Code /goal never finishes
videoDescription:
Claude Code /goal runs until a second model confirms your condition. That model has no tools.

The evaluator does not run commands and does not open files. It judges the condition against what already exists in the conversation. So a condition nobody proves inside the session never resolves, and there is no built-in turn limit to stop it.

Two things fix that. Name the command that produces the proof inside the condition, so the output lands in the conversation. Then add a stop clause, for example or stop after 20 turns.

Requires Claude Code 2.1.139 or newer.

videoTitle: Your uniq is not removing duplicates
videoDescription:
uniq compares each line only to the one directly before it. Duplicates
scattered through a file survive — silently, with no warning. That is not
a bug, it is the documented behaviour, and it has produced a lot of quietly
wrong numbers.

The fix:

  sort -u file.txt                          # dedupe properly
  sort file.txt | uniq -c | sort -rn | head # rank by frequency

And the trap almost nobody knows: combine -u with -k and sort compares only
the key field. Rows that differ everywhere else are thrown away without a word.

  sort -u -k1,1 data.tsv   # dedupes by field 1, not by the line

More practical engineering writing: https://www.alekseialeinikov.com
